text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An examinations board which has swindled thousands of unsuspecting students is not registered, Sunday Times investigations found.
- Hundreds of dignitaries grace wedding in Lagos on Saturday of the son of Lieutenant-General Oladipo Diya, the number two in Nigeria's military government.
- A secret cult known as Vikings claims responsibility for bloody clashes at Lagos university with rival group.
- Nigeria's two leading political parties, the UNCP and the DPN, are to levy their members wishing to contest governorship elections heavily in a bid to prune the number of aspirants.
- Succour is this week coming to former employees of the defunct Nigerian National Shippilng Line who will be paid nine months' arrears of their pension.
- The labour ministry is preparing for a national congress of the umbrella trade union body the Nigeria Labour Congress, following a directive to that effect from military ruler General Sani Abacha.
- Investors last week bought 162.8 million naira worth of equities on the Nigerian stock exchange compared to 278.5 million naira the week before.
- The federal government is considering slashing port charges to stem continous decline of shipping movement into Nigeria's seaports.
- Fears that western Nigeria will boycott next year's presidential election is the main reason for the proposal to shift governorship polls to next year, political sources say.
- The military administrator of the eastern Enugu state Colonel Sule Ahman says the opposition group NADECO planted the bombs last week in Onitsha town that killed five persons.
